clue.text: Frozen like a cake at the present time

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Frozen like a cake at the present time (4)' for ICED: 'Frozen' and 'like a cake' each define the answer, but no reading of 'at the present time' gives any letters or a third sense, so the clue as held looks corrupt
annotationWithheld.clue: Frozen like a cake at the present time

clue.text: Everybody giving expression of agreement that it is apparently satisfactory

parts.note: everybody means all, as in 'all were present'
'very well' is what one says when agreeing to something

explanation.surface: Everyone voices assent, suggesting that things seem to be fine.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is said of something that seems fine on the face of it but has a catch, so it is only seemingly acceptable.

indicators.note: first places the word at at the front of the charade, ahead of the other piece

parts.note: to tire someone is to weary or bother them

explanation.surface: Getting dressed is a nuisance to begin with.
explanation.definitionFit: Attire is a noun for clothing, and dress is used the same way for what one wears.

parts.note: read as a helpful favour, but also a plain description of making room or providing lodging for someone, which is an obliging act

explanation.surface: A request to be helpful.
explanation.definitionFit: To put someone up or meet their wishes is a kindly, helpful act, the very essence of doing a favour.

clue.text: Vehicle transported to ark going round island

indicators.note: going round tells us the rearranged letters encircle the island's letter
transported suggests the letters of to ark are carried off and set down in a new order

explanation.surface: A vehicle is carried to Noah's ark, passing around an island on the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transported' turns TO ARK into TROKA, and 'going round' puts I inside it after the O. A troika is a Russian carriage drawn by three horses abreast.
explanation.definitionFit: A troika is a Russian sledge or carriage pulled by a team of three horses, a horse-drawn conveyance.

clue.text: Soldiers with younger worker found it was vibrating

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, is a standard crossword abbreviation for soldiers
a son is of the younger generation relative to his parent
the ant is the crossword's stock worker, from the worker caste of the colony

explanation.surface: Troops, along with a junior labourer, discover something was shaking.
explanation.definitionFit: A resonant body hums and reverberates in sympathy with sound waves, so it is literally quivering.

clue.text: Not all a player has to learn

definitions.meaning: a portion rather than the whole
an actor's role, the lines a performer must memorise

explanation.surface: An actor has to memorise only some of the script.
explanation.definitionFit: A portion is less than the whole, and an actor's role is the script section he or she must commit to memory.

clue.text: Snap decision at end of race

definitions.meaning: a snap is a quick snapshot taken with a camera
a close race is settled by a camera image of the finishing line

explanation.surface: A judge makes a quick call as the runners cross the line.
explanation.definitionFit: A snap is an informal picture from a camera, and a 'photo finish' is how a dead heat is settled by a picture at the line.

indicators.note: during places the German's letter in the course of the journey, inside the word for it

parts.note: a ride is a journey on horseback or in a vehicle

explanation.surface: A German, partway through a trek, arrived at the summit.
explanation.definitionFit: A ridge is the long narrow crest of a hill or range, its uppermost line.

clue.text: Clio squirming about with inner pain

indicators.note: squirming suggests the name Clio wriggling into a new arrangement

parts.note: C stands for circa, Latin for about, as in a date given approximately

explanation.surface: A woman named Clio writhes with a stomach ache.
explanation.walkthrough: Clio looks like a real person, perhaps the Muse of history, but 'squirming' only shuffles her four letters, and C (circa) is the usual crossword shorthand for 'about'.
explanation.definitionFit: Colic is severe abdominal pain caused by spasm of the gut, a pain felt within the body.

clue.text: Angry, angry talk about pole entering dispute

indicators.note: entering tells us the pole's letter goes in between the other two pieces

parts.note: cross means angry, as in 'don't be cross with me'
'words' is angry talk, as in 'we had words'
S, south, is one of the two poles of the earth or a magnet

explanation.surface: A furious, bitter exchange about a pole leads to a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is only a joining word here. 'Pole' suggests a person from Poland, but it is the south pole; 'entering' puts its letter between the two angry pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To cross swords is to argue or clash with someone, an idiom drawn from fencing.

clue.text: Do take palindromic lady into port in Philippines

indicators.note: into shows the lady's name being placed inside the word do

parts.note: Ava is a woman's name that reads the same both ways

explanation.surface: An instruction to bring a woman with a symmetrical name into a Philippine harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: Davao is a major city and port on the island of Mindanao; 'into' signals the lady's name going inside the opening word.
explanation.definitionFit: Davao City is a large seaport on the Gulf of Davao in the southern Philippines.

parts.note: a counterfeiter manufactures banknotes, while the everyday sense is jotting things down

explanation.surface: A question about the activity of counterfeiters.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase normally means jotting down reminders, but read literally it describes counterfeiters producing paper money.

parts.note: a sports club from the shire, whose name is literally the shortened shire name plus the word for a shire

explanation.surface: A side from the English Midlands.
explanation.walkthrough: Notts is the usual short form of Nottinghamshire, an English county, and Notts County is the oldest professional football club in the world.
explanation.definitionFit: Notts County is a football club based in Nottingham, and its name is just the county's short form plus 'county'.

definitions.meaning: ivy is a climbing plant that clings to trunks
a small brown songbird that climbs up trunks probing bark for insects

explanation.surface: A bird belonging to a woman called Ivy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ivy' looks like a woman's name owning a pet; it is the climbing plant, and the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivy is a climber that clings to trunks, and the bird of that name scuttles up bark hunting insects.

parts.note: a print or print run is one edition of a book

explanation.surface: A southern newspaper edition has only a brief print run.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprint is a race or dash over a brief distance at full speed.

parts.note: Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet
after means following, as in 'the day after'

explanation.surface: Romeo comes along behind a ray of light, perhaps Juliet's.
explanation.definitionFit: A rafter is one of the sloping timbers supporting a roof, a structural joist.

indicators.note: included says the letters sit inside the run of the words many howlers

explanation.surface: Lots of glaring blunders were thrown in at random.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something anyhow means doing it carelessly or without order, in a random way.

clue.text: New gear going round put on sweaters

indicators.note: going round shows the kit surrounding the letter for new

parts.note: kit is gear or equipment, as in sports kit
to wear clothes is to have them put on

explanation.surface: Fresh outfits wrapped around a pullover someone dons.
explanation.definitionFit: Knitwear is clothing made from knitted yarn, of which jumpers and cardigans are typical examples.

definitions.meaning: a whim, an odd notion or fad
a musical note lasting one beat, called a quarter note in America

explanation.surface: An elaborate musical symbol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' looks like an adjective describing the note; it is a noun for a whimsical idea.
explanation.definitionFit: A crotchet is both a perverse whim and the musical symbol for a quarter note.

clue.text: The south African spoon-bender found in books

parts.note: A is an abbreviation for African
Uri Geller is the entertainer famous for bending spoons

explanation.surface: A South African psychic who bends cutlery is discovered in some volumes.
explanation.walkthrough: Uri Geller is the Israeli-British performer known for apparently bending spoons by mind power.
explanation.definitionFit: Thesauri, the plural of thesaurus, are reference volumes listing synonyms.

clue.text: Mum, after one, is able to find container

indicators.note: after places the word for mum behind the letter for one

parts.note: a means one, as in 'a dozen'
'mum' means keep quiet, and 'sh' is the call for silence
can means is able, as in 'she can swim'

explanation.surface: Mother, following someone, manages to locate a box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mum' looks like a mother; here it means silent, as in 'keep mum', so it gives the hushing SH.
explanation.definitionFit: An ashcan is an American dustbin, a receptacle for rubbish and ashes.

definitions.meaning: an odd number cannot be halved into whole numbers

explanation.surface: A question whether something rough-looking is strange.
explanation.definitionFit: Rough ground is not level, and an odd number such as seven cannot be split into two equal whole parts.

parts.note: notedly hints at musical notes, so this is a score marking that tells players to slow down

explanation.surface: Something famous is gradually decelerating.
explanation.definitionFit: Rallentando is the Italian musical direction for gradually decreasing tempo.

clue.text: Maps for a sailor to bring up

indicators.note: in a down light, to bring up is to raise the letters so they read from bottom to top

parts.note: a salt is an old sailor, as in 'old salt'

explanation.surface: Charts for a seaman to raise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to bring up' works because this is a down entry: the sailor's word is read upwards, and the 'old salt' sense of sailor is a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: An atlas is a book of charts, a bound collection of maps.

indicators.note: in shows the answer sits within the words basil has arrived, across their breaks

explanation.surface: A man named Basil has reached a capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: Lhasa is the capital of Tibet.
explanation.definitionFit: Lhasa is the chief city and seat of government of Tibet.

clue.text: Affect greatly enclosed area in town

indicators.note: in places the enclosure inside the letters standing for the town

parts.note: UD stands for urban district, an old British local-government unit covering a town
a pen is a small enclosure for animals

explanation.surface: A fenced space in a town has a big impact.
explanation.walkthrough: An urban district (UD) was a former English and Welsh local council area covering a town, so 'town' gives UD.
explanation.definitionFit: To upend someone is figuratively to overturn them or have a dramatic effect on them, as shocking news can.

indicators.note: said shows the poet's name is spoken, producing a word that sounds the same

parts.note: John Donne was the English metaphysical poet

explanation.surface: Someone claims a poet is worn out.
explanation.definitionFit: Done in the sense of tired out, as in 'I'm absolutely done', means utterly spent.

clue.text: Les can move to harbour leaving no sign of any stubble

definitions.text: leaving no sign of any stubble

indicators.note: move tells us the letters of les can are to be shifted about into a new order

parts.note: a haven is a harbour or safe anchorage

explanation.surface: A man called Les is able to relocate to a port, leaving his chin smooth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'move' turns LES CAN into CLEANS, followed by HAVEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A clean-shaven face has had all its whiskers removed with a razor.

parts.note: to tie is to fasten or secure
in can mean available, as in fashionable or at home and ready to receive callers

explanation.surface: Fasten an accessible connection.
explanation.definitionFit: A tie-in is a connection or association between two things, such as a film and its book.

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, a clothing label meaning very large
SA is the abbreviation for Saudi Arabia

explanation.surface: A large man from Saudi Arabia.
explanation.walkthrough: Ossa is the Latin plural of os, bone, used in anatomy.
explanation.definitionFit: In anatomy the Latin word os means a skeletal element, and its plural is used for several of them.

definitions.meaning: like a bee, read jokily as 'having a sting'

explanation.surface: A question whether being miserly is the same as being bee-like.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the word as sting plus -y, 'having a sting', which is what being bee-like might mean.
explanation.definitionFit: A miser is tight-fisted, and a bee carries a sting, so 'sting-y' is a whimsical way to say bee-like.
